Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

gristmillr 0.0.0.9000

  • grist_write_options() gains parse. Set parse = FALSE to send noparse=true and store values as sent instead of letting Grist parse them to match column types.

  • grist_workspaces(), grist_docs() and grist_workspace_create() use your only org when the server has no “current” org, as with Grist Desktop.

  • Functions that delete or overwrite things (grist_doc_delete(), grist_workspace_delete(), grist_webhook_delete(), grist_snapshot_restore(), grist_snapshots_remove() and grist_doc_history_truncate()) take ask. ask = FALSE skips the prompt; the default prompts when interactive and errors in a script.

  • Initial development version with document handles (grist_doc()), options objects and grist_request() for building authenticated requests.

  • grist_tables(), grist_table_create(), grist_columns(), grist_columns_add() and grist_columns_modify() read and change a document’s schema.

  • grist_records(), grist_records_add(), grist_records_update(), grist_records_insert(), grist_records_upsert() and grist_records_delete() read and write records with a convert enum ("auto", "basic" or "raw"). The writing functions take data first and return it, so they can be piped, and grist_records_add() returns it with the new row IDs in an id column. grist_sql() and grist_count() run SQL queries.

  • grist_doc_create(), grist_doc_info(), grist_doc_update(), grist_doc_move(), grist_doc_delete() and grist_doc_restore() manage documents, and grist_orgs(), grist_workspaces(), grist_docs() and grist_workspace_*() list and manage orgs and workspaces. Deleting takes mode = "trash" or "permanent" and asks before deleting (ask = NULL, the default; ask = FALSE skips the prompt).

  • grist_doc_download() saves a document or table as .grist, Excel, CSV, TSV or DSV, and grist_table_schema() returns a table’s Table Schema.

  • grist_resolve_refs() looks up display values for Ref and RefList columns, and vignette("joining-tables") shows how to join tables.

  • grist_attachments(), grist_attachment_info(), grist_attachments_upload() and grist_attachment_download() list, upload and download attachments.

  • grist_webhooks(), grist_webhook_create(), grist_webhook_update(), grist_webhook_delete() and grist_webhook_queue_clear() manage webhooks.

  • grist_columns() returns column descriptions, and grist_columns_add(), grist_columns_modify() and grist_table_create() can set them.

  • grist_doc_history(), grist_snapshots() and grist_doc_compare() read a document’s action history, snapshots and changes between states.

  • grist_snapshot_restore(), grist_snapshots_remove() and grist_doc_history_truncate() restore a snapshot and remove snapshots or old history, after confirmation.

  • grist_doc() and grist_request_options() gain an api_key argument, a string or a function returning one. String keys are held in session memory and never serialised with the object.

  • grist_doc_info() returns created_at and updated_at. grist_orgs() now returns its timestamps as POSIXct in UTC rather than strings.

  • vignette("gristmillr") is a getting-started guide.

  • grist_records_update(), grist_records_upsert() and grist_records_insert() match records on key columns (by), with unmatched and multiple enums as in dplyr’s rows_*() functions. None of them delete records.

  • grist_records() no longer fails on an empty table with untyped (Any) columns.

  • grist_export() writes a document’s tables to Parquet, CSV or JSON files and a data-dict data-dict.yaml that records column types, descriptions and references. grist_import() creates tables from such a dictionary and its data files, converting foreign keys to Ref columns, and can load data prepared outside Grist. Both need the yaml12 package, and nanoparquet for Parquet files.

  • vignette("migrating-data") explains how to move tables in and out of Grist with grist_export() and grist_import().

  • grist_doc_import() creates a document from a .grist, .csv, .xlsx or .json file.

Developed by Eli Pousson.
